https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/1266945260400152591/1458694715913277585/Desktop_2026.01.08_-_12.31.23.01.mp4?ex=696092d1&is=695f4151&hm=8ece8b8c2c23f6b8d5fcf3e3d4a6f0dd5a59e21e32acac72718704325c79f9a6&
voxov 2026-01-08 12:00 AM

Secondary Objectives:

I feel as if it would provide no need for players to actually do the secondary objectives anyways. The primary issue is that the only thing that you gain from doing the secondary objectives is money and experience. There was previously not a lot for players to want to engage in after generators before, but now we currently have an actual reason to want to engage in gameplay and want to use your abilities and such which provide all the previously explained and Malice, which is likely the main goal of most people to begin with. I feel that us going forward with that idea will be a fun idea at first, but will likely go unnoticed after weeks to come as there is no initiative to do it aside from the money and experience which you can already get from using your abilities. People want to have the feeling and push to do something, but with secondary objectives, doing something that does something so much further less than what using your abilities does feels like it would be a waste. That is my reason as to why we shouldn't advance with that, and I think our resources would be better fit towards something else rather than that.

Gamemodes:

Reason I see no point in going with gamemodes. Currently right now we struggle as is balancing our default mode, where there is a lot of tiny details and tweaks that need to be done, and as is the default base game still suffers. Advancing forward with gamemodes takes away from the core gameplay and point of the game, which also adds on a huge issue with balancers where we already struggle as is with the base mode, adding more onto that pile while we still need to prioritize polishing the core gameplay as is likely isn't the best move.

UI Overhaul:

I believe I have said this before, but this is a huge thing to take on. The main issue that I have is, while with the current UI that we have has its flaws, it is something we can still polish and fix up, it is quite amazing already as is, and already has so much soul. Undertaking this kind of task is quite a problem since right now as I have mentioned in my other points, we have a lot of other core issues that the game suffers from. If we were to do the complete UI overhaul, we take a huge risk as to if it will work well with people or it will flop. If it completely flops then it is a huge waste of time, that could have been put towards other things to advance the game in a better direction. The UI we have is fine, we can work off it and improve it to make things better. Additionally, I believe I have mentioned this but its a difficult task for us programmers to undertake, we already have a lot of responsibilities, and completely rewriting something to include new functionality, and maintaining the current structure is a huge task. These are mostly the things I looked at and feel that we would be prioritizing our resources into the wrong places. We have a fantastic team, but we have to figure out the right places to put things that will improve the game at its core. I think that is the main problems that I have with all of this, and I do hope you understand. I do quite like the bulk of the changes listed within here and I am fully onboard with structuring out a timeline with these changes and going forward with it. Though, before we were to advance with anything, there is a lot more that needs to be considered within the document that needs to be explained and highlighted. (edited)

@ composers Me and Eggo have written guidelines for music. These guidelines include general traits each killer theme possesses along with the typical map/lms jargon, we'd like for you all to review it and give us your thoughts so we can make it even clearer for those who we may work with in the future on themes. You can find the guidelines in the music spreadsheet. We'd also like to note that you will no longer need to come to us to review emote music. The person implementing the music (likely one of the skin leads or the animation lead) will check for issues such as profane lyrics, volume, or other issues that would prevent the audio from being ingame; we, the music leads, may give commentary on the music itself, but they would not affect whether the music is implemented. Additionally, a separate forum has been made for emote music to separate it from the standard review system we have. (edited)

You can find the guidelines in the music spreadsheet. We'd also like to note that you will no longer need to come to us to review emote music. The person implementing the music (likely one of the skin leads or the animation lead) will check for issues such as profane lyrics, volume, or other issues that would prevent the audio from being ingame; we, the music leads, may give commentary on the music itself, but they would not affect whether the music is implemented. Additionally, a separate forum has been made for emote music to separate it from the standard review system we have. (edited)
